title: Image-derived knowledge
description: Structured notes transcribed from five project reference images. These are visual observations, not independent validation of the named tools or research claims.

items.title: Infrastructure as Code — core concepts
observations: The image groups IaC artifacts into templates, scripts, and policies.
It names Ansible, Terraform, Chef, and Puppet as tools.
It depicts network, application, storage, security, and cloud infrastructure as infrastructure domains.

items.title: Infrastructure automation tool landscape
observations: The diagram places Terraform, Ansible, Chef, Puppet, AWS CloudFormation, Azure Resource Templates, and Jenkins around the IaC topic.
It also labels New Relic, Zabbix, and Nagios, indicating monitoring/observability tools in the wider landscape.

items.title: IaC landscape cheatsheet
items.confidence: visual transcription; fine print may be incomplete
observations: The cheatsheet groups containerization, container orchestration, configuration management, and infrastructure-as-code tools.
Docker is shown in the containerization area and Kubernetes in the orchestration area.
The infrastructure-as-code section depicts developer workflows connecting code, pull requests, automation servers, and cloud or on-premises infrastructure.
The configuration-management section depicts playbooks/inventory and server provisioning workflows.

items.title: Context engineering visualised
items.confidence: visual transcription; source is a screenshot and some labels are small
observations: The diagram distinguishes short-term memory from long-term memory.
Long-term memory examples include MCP servers, databases, RAG, and vector search.
The flow connects user input, prompt/context, an agent, action tools, and an answer.
The diagram presents memory and tool use as parts of a repeated agent interaction loop.

items.title: Agentic full-stack development and evaluation
items.confidence: visual transcription; details summarized at diagram level
observations: The figure contrasts FullStack-Dev, FullStack-Learn, and FullStack-Bench.
It depicts planning, repository exploration, coding agents, information gathering, trajectory/back-translation, and agent trajectories.
The benchmark area separates frontend, backend, and database test cases and corresponding judge agents.

interpretation.claim: The images together suggest a knowledge workflow connecting infrastructure automation, agent context/memory, repository-aware coding, and testing.
interpretation.rationale: This is a synthesis across multiple images, not a statement explicitly made by any single image.

limitations: DIRECT means the item is visibly represented in the image; it does not verify that the depiction is current or technically complete.
INDIRECT marks a synthesis or inference across image observations.
Text too small to read confidently is summarized rather than reconstructed.
These notes are a starter dataset; they do not replace source documents, citations, or technical validation.
